readings: Sum expense.cost per link_to_budget, so each budget line that has at least one expense gets a total. Take the average of those totals across only the budget lines that have expenses, and keep the lines whose total is above it. For those lines, what is the average total, how many expenses do they have altogether, and what is the average amount by which their totals exceed that average?

Sum expense.cost per link_to_budget. Define the average spend per budget line as the total expense cost divided by the number of all rows in the budget table, counting budget lines with no expenses as zero spend. Keep the budget lines whose expense total is above that average. For those lines, what is the average total, how many expenses do they have altogether, and what is the average amount by which their totals exceed that average?
queries:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT link_to_budget, SUM(cost) AS total, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM expense
    WHERE link_to_budget IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY link_to_budget
),
a AS (
    SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t
)
SELECT AVG(t.total) AS avg_total,
       SUM(t.cnt) AS total_expenses,
       AVG(t.total - a.av) AS avg_excess
FROM t, a
WHERE t.total > a.av;
WITH totals AS (
    SELECT link_to_budget, SUM(cost) AS total, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM expense
    GROUP BY link_to_budget
),
avg_spend AS (
    SELECT (SELECT SUM(cost) FROM expense) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM budget) AS avg_val
)
SELECT AVG(t.total) AS average_total,
       SUM(t.cnt) AS total_expenses,
       AVG(t.total - a.avg_val) AS average_excess
FROM totals t, avg_spend a
WHERE t.total > a.avg_val;
